beats.say: That squirrel in your park... knows exactly where its nuts are *buried.*
You've heard they *forget* where they hide them.
But one squirrel can bury up to *3,000* nuts in a single autumn.
It builds a *mental map*, with trees and bushes as landmarks.
In one field test, grey squirrels dug within *five centimetres* of their nuts... after twenty days.
Some even sort their nuts by *type.* Walnuts here, almonds there.
And when someone's watching, they *fake* a burial to fool thieves.
One researcher says they're strategizing *quite a lot.*
Some nuts do stay in the ground... often *abandoned*, not forgotten.
And those nuts grow into new *trees.*
If you feed them, use *unsalted* nuts, like hazelnuts in the shell.
Just a little, every few days, so they keep *foraging.*
So next time you see a squirrel digging in the grass... remember:
